title: Credit Transactions: The Creditors Journal
summary: Buying on credit, creditors as liabilities, the original invoice as source document, recording credit purchases in the Creditors Journal, paying creditors and posting to the ledger.

notes.text: Businesses often buy trading stock and other items from suppliers on credit and pay later, usually within 30 to 60 days. A supplier to whom the business owes money is a **creditor**. Creditors are a **liability**.

rows: The business can sell the goods before paying for them
Interest may be charged on late payments
Helps cash flow, especially for new businesses
Too much debt can lead to financial trouble
Builds a credit record with suppliers
Discounts for paying cash may be lost

notes.text: When buying on credit, the business receives the **original invoice** from the supplier. This is the source document for the **Creditors Journal (CJ)**.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Selling on credit: the business issues the invoice and keeps the **duplicate** (Debtors Journal). Buying on credit: the business receives the **original** invoice (Creditors Journal).

notes.caption: Creditors Journal of Kasi Fashions, April 2025

notes.text: Check: Trading stock + Stationery + Sundry = 18 500 + 350 + 500 = 19 350 = Creditors control ✓.
Each invoice is also posted to the individual creditor's account in the **Creditors Ledger**, so the business knows how much it owes each supplier.
When the business pays a creditor, the payment is recorded in the **CPJ** in the Bank column and the **Creditors control** column. The amount owed decreases.
